131. People with good intuition, people with bad intuition (2)
Amela, a mercenary from the Gaipa Military Region, was a character with very little information known about her compared to her reputation as one of the top three mercenaries.
Everyone praised her anonymity, and special articles about Amela were published quite often.
Amela carried out at least one war-related request every year, and it was natural that she always brought about "great" results.

However, those pieces of information were hollow. There were very few reporters who had met Amela in person or had seen her reveal herself in official ceremonies, so the articles could be considered purely based on imagination.
In his previous life, Jin had also encountered the character Amela through such articles.
But there was just one time. His master, Valeria Hister, had mentioned Amela.
- Amela wears the skins of the people she has killed? There are often strange articles about this person.
- Isn't that because there is no particular penalty for reporters publishing false articles?
- That's true. However, this person would be completely unaware of the fact that reporters are writing such articles about her, or how her image is being perceived by the people. Right?
- Completely unaware?
- Yeah, she belonged to a category of people who were seriously uninterested in worldly affairs. From what I saw. And she was incredibly pure.
-...Pure? Wearing human skin seems like nonsense to me, but it's clear that her war abilities are extremely superior. Can she be pure?
- Being pure doesn't always have a good meaning. Anyway, if you're done with your tea, let's go train.
That conversation took place on a day in his previous life, when they had breakfast together and looked through the newspapers.
At that time, he didn't think Amela was particularly important, so he didn't give it any special meaning.
'Being pure doesn't always have a good meaning...'
Thinking about it now, the meaning of those words was obvious.
Amela is a person with a vague concept of good and evil.
"Why do you think that?"
Valkas asked one last question. He wanted to hear the reason why Amela should be captured and contained.
"The fact that the Black Knights and the Ghost Corps have formed an alliance with me."
"It's not an alliance, but a relationship between a lord and a vassal. There's no need to choose your words so carefully considering the feelings of Lata or me."

"Now everyone knows that fact. I actually wanted to keep it hidden until our forces became stronger. Anyway, there are now only two remaining major neutral forces in the world. Mercenary Amela and Bighung."
"That's right."
"Bighung's alliance with me has not yet been revealed to the world, but the major forces should have some idea."
"Well... the people would recognize it as more than just an alliance, but as a prospective family. The rumors of a marriage between you and Bighung's princess have been going around for a long time."

"The only one left is Amela. Anyone who captures her will be in an awkward position. I haven't been active recently, so I'm just now stepping up, but other forces are already trying to make contact with Amela. If we're unlucky, she may have already joined someone else."
Due to Jin's recent actions, the world's balance of power had shifted.
Long-neutral forces had joined the 12th generation of Runcan, and tensions had escalated among the major powers.
Those in the gray area had been making choices. Which side they would take. The neutrals were disappearing one by one.
"The likelihood of her already being affiliated with someone is low, my lord. She's quite an elusive figure."
"Do you know her well?"
"I'd say we're relatively close by Amela's standards. By normal standards, we've coincidentally encountered each other on the battlefield a few times and shared a couple of meals."
As both Amela and Valkas were famous mercenaries, they had been on the same battlefield with different contracts.
Valkas narrowed his brow as he recalled those moments.
"Do you know, my lord? Amela doesn't have her own mercenary group."
"Yes, she works alone."
"Despite that, whenever I've encountered Amela on the battlefield, I've never been able to defeat her."
"Are you saying that there's such a gap between you and Amela?"
"It's not between me and Amela, but between the Black King's Squad and Amela."
Jin's eyes widened.
"What do you mean...?"

"As much as I hate to admit it, at least in terms of war execution, Amela is superior to the entire Black King's Squad, including myself. It might be a different story in a one-on-one duel, but I'm confident. I never had the opportunity to challenge her."
Valkas locked eyes with Jin as he continued.

"In other words, we must make Amela one of your people, my lord. Temporarily fighting with a different employer is a completely different issue from becoming an outright enemy. If I think she's going to be a personal enemy, I might consider killing her."
At his resolute words, Jin nodded.
"I understand what you mean. Our top priority is to figure out what Amela wants. Do you know anything specific?"
"Exploration."
"Exploration?"

"Amela has spent her entire life wandering and exploring the world. After the battle, we had a meal together and she casually mentioned that she was searching for something with great passion... but she didn't tell me exactly what it was."
If only we can figure out what that is, we can easily make her one of my people.
Such a strong intuition crossed my mind.
'She has little interest in the world's affairs, to the point of being serious. Perhaps the way her master described her in her past life is because Amela is a person immersed in her own goals.'
It was necessary to ask Valeria, too, if she knew Amela. It would be nice for them to go together.
"Anyway, we should meet and have a conversation."
"Yes, my lord. And taking the Proch siblings along might be helpful."
"Lata and Fey?"
"When the three of us met on the battlefield in the past, Amela seemed to find those friends oddly cute. Lata seemed quite disgusted, though."
It was hard to imagine someone finding Lata cute, but it seemed there would be no harm in bringing them along.
"Understood."
"Then I'll go back to supervising the construction. If Amela is cooperative, please pass on my regards."
As Valkas left, as if waiting, someone came to find Jin.
It was Gilly.
"My lord."
"Yes, Gilly."
Jin had also noticed for a while, or more precisely, recently, that Gilly seemed to want to talk to him about something.
He had been waiting for her to sort out her thoughts and speak up.
'She seemed constantly troubled because of Dox.'

Even when Macrogas did not greet her after she became a knight, and when Dox, whom she had saved, silently left (in fact, Jin felt like he had received a message to raise the level of alert as a gift).
Gilly acted as if she had committed a sin.
"I'm worried about what to do if my knight... no, the Black Knight doesn't obey my lord's orders."
"Why would Gilly worry about that?"
"Well, my family's."
Gilly paused for a moment and then continued in a less confident voice.
"Because he's a person from my family... "
"The Black Knight doesn't care about family. And as I said before..."
He barely suppressed his rising anger and stopped speaking.
Of course, his anger was not directed at Gilly but at Macrogas, who was making her feel small.
"I won't have any particular grudge against Macrogas. As long as they don't openly harm Gilly. So don't worry."
Jin couldn't control his emotions well when it came to Gilly.
Although he said not to worry, Jin's gaze was soaked in deep resentment, as if it wouldn't be strange to wipe out the Macrogas family at any moment.
Gilly couldn't bear the pain of that fact and couldn't raise her head, and Jin realized the fact a beat later.
'Ah.'
It was always difficult to practice putting Gilly's feelings first, even though he knew he should.
But Jin knew.
He remembered it vividly.
When he was exiled in his past life, and Gilly was facing the same fate...
Macrogas did not offer a helping hand to Gilly. With the influence Macrogas had in Huphester, they could have helped Gilly as much as they wanted.
Of course, helping her become a knight again might have been impossible, but at least they could have prevented her from facing a lonely and miserable death.
That was the reason Jin was angry with the Macrogas family.

"Well, whether the Black Knight obeys that command or not, he has no choice but to give me meaningful information. If he doesn't obey, I can assume that all active Black Knights are involved with Ricarten. If he obeys, he's digging up Joshua's secrets for me instead."
Jin said, suppressing his anger once more.
"Besides, Joshua will no longer trust that Black Knight, so there's a high chance he'll eventually become my man. As long as I don't get killed by Joshua before becoming the head of the family."
"I'll save him."
"Excuse me?"

"If it seems like Dox will be killed by Joshua, I'll save him. As I said, he's not a knight of Macrogas, but a Black Knight. He's the most important force of the family, so I won't let him die in vain. That's why I saved him this time as well."
When Gilly bowed, Jin shrugged his shoulders.

"You understand now that there's nothing for Gilly to worry about, right? I'll be heading straight to Gaipa Highway, so please get everything ready. It's been a while since I felt Gilly taking care of me."
"Understood, my lord. I'll get everything prepared quickly."
